prompt: Roadmap III, Prompt 226 Part A: transit timing variations, the O-C diagram and the super-period (tranche T3 by D-R10-207-01)
committed: before any file of js/kernels/ttv, the validator, the oracle, the panels or the lesson existed. The cases, the definitions and every bound below were fixed here first.
rule: A crossed bound is a failed leg, recorded in failed-legs.json and left failing; only Carl resets one. A leg that cannot be measured, or whose data was never supplied, is NOT RUN and says why. An amendment is recorded in 'amendments' with its reason; the original bound stays in 'checks' and keeps failing.
disclosure: One exploratory probe was run before this file was committed, on a system like S1 (P 10 and 20 d, 3e-5 each, circular start, ratio 2.02 and 2.06): the engine and a scipy DOP853 integration agreed on the first transit times to 3e-5 d at P/2000 steps, and the first-order amplitude formula agreed with the integrated amplitude to about 4 percent (inner) and 16 percent (outer, whose g coefficient is small so the free-eccentricity term matters more). The bounds below were chosen from the physics (the integrator's second-order phase error, the formula's neglect of free eccentricity, the coverage of a binomial count) and are not tuned to pass.

constants.timeUnit: 1 code time unit is 1 day. Newtonian scale invariance: only the period ratio, the mass ratio mu = m / M* and the phases matter, so the engine (G = 1, star 1000 mass units) and the oracle (same units) are compared in these units; a stated physical star (1 solar mass) turns mu = 3e-5 into 10 Earth masses.
constants.observer: along +y of the orbital plane: a transit is the moment the planet's x equals the star's x with the planet at larger y (the plane is seen edge-on; the impact parameter of the light-curve template is a separate input).

S4.what: S1 observed for 250 d, less than one super-period

systems.start: Both planets start on circular astrocentric orbits (period from Kepler's third law with M* + m), the star at rest at the origin; the free eccentricity this leaves is part of what the amplitude relation neglects (see A4).

engine.note: the second-order phase error of this step is part of B1's budget

oracle.method: scipy solve_ivp DOP853, rtol 1e-12, atol 1e-14, event on the sky-plane x separation with the planet in front; no Gravitas code

lightCurve.note: A 2-minute cadence, 400 ppm per point, a planet of 2.5 percent of the star's radius (6.3e-4 depth). The template is the quadratic-law transit of js/inference/transit.js with these shape values known; mid-time and a baseline are fitted (js/inference core, 150 uncertainties).

definitions.O-C: O - C = T_n - (T0 + n P) with T0 and P the weighted least-squares linear ephemeris of the same transit times.
definitions.superPeriod: P_super = 1 / | j / P2 - (j - 1) / P1 | (Lithwick, Xie & Wu 2012, ApJ 761, 122, eq. 1) with P1, P2 the MEAN periods of the linear ephemerides.
definitions.amplitude: |V| = P1 mu2 / (pi j^(2/3) (j-1)^(1/3) |Delta|) |f| for the inner planet and |V'| = P2 mu1 / (pi j |Delta|) |g| for the outer one, Z_free = 0, with f and g from the Laplace coefficients (Murray & Dermott 1999, eqs 8.?? f27, f31; the 2:1 values -1.1905 and 0.4284, the 3:2 values -2.0252 and 2.4840), Delta = (P2 / P1)(j - 1)/j - 1.
definitions.measuredAmplitude: the amplitude of cos and sin terms fitted together with a straight line to the transit times at the period P_super, in days
definitions.signal: kernel verdict 'signal' when the chi-square of the O-C about zero (n - 2 degrees of freedom) has a one-sided p below 0.01; otherwise 'no TTV signal above noise'. 'unresolved' when the baseline is shorter than 1.5 super-periods, in which case no super-period is reported.
definitions.coverage: |t_measured - t_true| / sigma_stated, t_true the engine's transit time, over every measured transit of every ensemble member

checks.what: the engine's O-C period of S1's inner planet, fitted on a grid, against the cited super-period of the measured mean periods
S1's inner and outer O-C periods agree with each other
first-order amplitude formula (Z_free = 0) against the engine's measured amplitude, S1 inner and outer, S2 inner and outer

limits.note: the neglected free eccentricity enters the outer planet at order (3/2) Z / (Delta g), larger than for the inner one

checks.what: the Laplace-coefficient f and g against the published values for 2:1 and 3:2
engine O-C against the oracle's O-C, maximum absolute difference after each removes its own linear ephemeris (S1 and S2, both planets)
oracle self-check: its O-C at rtol 1e-10 against rtol 1e-12
the kernel's super-period and amplitudes against the oracle's own implementation of the same two relations (S1, S2)
the kernel's linear ephemeris against the oracle's numpy weighted least squares on the oracle's transit times
coverage of the stated 1-sigma transit-time intervals, S1 (both planets, 20 noise realisations)
mean and standard deviation of the normalised time error
S3 (far from resonance): verdict 'no TTV signal above noise' in at least this fraction of 40 noise realisations, both planets
S1: verdict 'signal' in at least this fraction of the same 40 realisations
stated sigma understated by 2: the per-transit fit-quality flag is raised for at least this fraction of transits
S4 (baseline under 1.5 super-periods): status 'unresolved', no super-period
a pair not near a first-order resonance (ratio 2.7, Delta to 2:1 above 0.1): the relation refuses and names why
a pair inside the resonance width (|Delta| below (mu1 + mu2)^(2/3)): the sinusoid relation refuses and says to use the engine

a published Kepler system's O-C from its published transit times (Kepler-9 b and c, Holczer et al. 2016): the super-period fitted to the O-C against the cited relation from the data's own mean periods
checks.supply: needs the published times, supplied by the coordinator under a recorded rights decision; NOT RUN if never supplied

notClaimed: A planet mass from a TTV amplitude: Part B (docs/ttv-mass-gate) decides whether any mass bound ships, and with what degeneracy.
TTVs inside the resonance width, from three or more planets, from a third body, from light-travel time or from apsidal precession: the sinusoid relation is stated for two planets outside the width.
A three-dimensional geometry: the engine is planar, so the light curve's impact parameter is an input of the template, not a result of the orbit.
